scope: Local explanations of the native problem contracts; graph data answers use computed facts instead.

sections.title: Result guarantees
sections.text: Exact means the declared mathematical result is established when execution completes. A heuristic does not guarantee an optimum. Numerical results have their declared tolerances; stochastic and learned results have different guarantees. Complete output means no requested result rows were omitted; it does not make a heuristic exact. Check each problem's quality and solution_quality contract.

sections.title: k-core and k-truss
sections.text: A k-core retains vertices with at least k neighbors inside the remaining subgraph. A k-truss retains edges supported by at least k minus two triangles inside the remaining subgraph. Both use repeated peeling in this library; core membership measures vertex degree, while truss membership measures triangle support for edges.

sections.title: Maximal and maximum cliques
sections.text: Every pair of vertices in a clique is connected. A maximal clique cannot be extended by adding another vertex. A maximum clique has the largest size of any clique in the graph. All maximum cliques are maximal, but maximal cliques can be smaller than the maximum.

sections.title: Bicliques and communities
sections.text: A biclique has two sides with every possible connection between the sides. In a review graph, its Users all connect to its Businesses. A community groups vertices according to a declared objective such as modularity or the constant Potts model; it does not require every pair or every cross-side pair to be connected. Maximal bicliques enumerate inclusion-maximal complete cross-side groups, while community detection returns a partition.

sections.title: Degree and PageRank
sections.text: Degree counts direct neighbors with the declared direction and normalization. PageRank computes random-walk scores with restart and dangling-node rules, so a vertex's score depends on the wider connection structure. Degree and PageRank answer different questions and can rank the same vertices differently.

sections.title: Using a recorded field as a weight
sections.text: Promoting review stars to edge.weight makes the recorded rating the numeric edge value. Its meaning depends on the chosen problem: a larger random-walk weight attracts more transition mass, while a larger shortest-path length makes that edge more costly. A rating must not be silently treated as a distance, probability or capacity. Confirm the field and objective first; each problem still checks its weight constraints.
